summary.title: HelixPay: Customer Payment Data Threat Model
summary.description: STRIDE model derived from the whiteboard attack tree. Attacker goal: steal real customer payment data from HelixPay. Attack paths: phishing, weak MFA + 16 admin accounts, Log4j to payment server, Jenkins to privilege escalation, MITM, lateral movement, staging API exposed, AWS publicly exposed, security misconfiguration.

data.name: Customer
data.description: End user paying via HelixPay (target of phishing)

threats.title: Customer phishing / credential theft
threats.description: Attacker phishes customers to obtain credentials and impersonates them via the App or API Gateway.
threats.mitigation: Phishing-resistant MFA (passkeys/FIDO2), risk-based login, anti-phishing education, transaction signing/step-up auth, anomaly detection.

threats.title: XSS / client-side injection
threats.description: XSS (noted on the whiteboard as 'XSS evidence') lets an attacker run script in the customer's session and steal tokens or payment data.
threats.mitigation: Output encoding, strict CSP, HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, input validation, SAST/DAST in CI.

threats.title: Insecure data exposure in client
threats.description: Sensitive payment data cached or logged on the device or in the browser.
threats.mitigation: No sensitive data in local storage/logs, tokenise card data, certificate pinning on mobile.

threats.title: Man-in-the-middle on client traffic
threats.description: MITM on untrusted networks intercepts or alters traffic.
threats.mitigation: TLS 1.2+/HSTS, certificate pinning, disallow downgrade.

data.name: API Gateway
data.description: Entry point for all API calls

threats.title: Stolen/forged API tokens
threats.description: Attacker replays or forges tokens obtained via phishing or MITM.
threats.mitigation: Short-lived OAuth2/JWT, mTLS for service clients, token binding, revocation.

threats.title: Missing rate limiting / abuse
threats.description: Flooding or credential stuffing exhausts the gateway.
threats.mitigation: Rate limiting, WAF, bot protection, autoscaling.

threats.title: Broken authorisation (BOLA/IDOR)
threats.description: Customers access other customers' payment data via object-ID manipulation.
threats.mitigation: Server-side authorisation on every request, schema validation, API security tests.

threats.title: Log4j (Log4Shell) remote code execution
threats.description: Vulnerable Log4j allows RCE via attacker-controlled log input, giving a path from Log4j to the payment server and the DB.
threats.mitigation: Upgrade Log4j to a patched version, SBOM and dependency scanning (SCA), disable JNDI lookups, egress filtering, run with least privilege.

threats.title: Insufficient audit logging of payments
threats.description: Payment actions can't be traced reliably to a user or system.
threats.mitigation: Tamper-evident centralised logging, immutable audit trail, NTP sync.

threats.title: Sensitive data written to logs
threats.description: Card data or tokens end up in Log4j output.
threats.mitigation: Log scrubbing/masking, PCI DSS logging rules.

data.name: Customer Payment DB
data.description: Stores real customer payment data (the attacker's goal)

threats.title: Unauthorised DB access (central attack node)
threats.description: Multiple paths converge on DB access: compromised admin accounts, lateral movement, exposed AWS resources, payment server compromise, staging API.
threats.mitigation: Network segmentation, private subnets/no public endpoints, DB-level least privilege, JIT/PAM for admin access, DB activity monitoring, tokenisation.

threats.title: Unencrypted or weakly protected data at rest
threats.description: Exfiltrated storage or backups reveal payment data.
threats.mitigation: Encryption at rest with KMS/HSM keys, key rotation, field-level encryption, backup protection.

threats.title: Data tampering by privileged user
threats.description: Unauthorised modification of payment records.
threats.mitigation: Integrity controls, change auditing, four-eyes approval for admin changes.

data.name: Staging / API Server
data.description: Staging API server, exposed to the internet

threats.title: Exposed staging server with prod data or credentials
threats.description: Publicly reachable staging API with weak controls gives an attacker a route to the DB.
threats.mitigation: Remove public exposure, IP allow-listing/VPN, no production data or secrets in staging, separate AWS accounts.

threats.title: Security misconfiguration
threats.description: Default configs, debug endpoints or open ports.
threats.mitigation: Hardening baselines (CIS), IaC scanning, config drift detection.

threats.title: Publicly exposed cloud resources
threats.description: Misconfigured S3 buckets, security groups or DB endpoints are open to the internet.
threats.mitigation: Block Public Access, AWS Config/Security Hub rules, CSPM, least-privilege IAM, SCPs.

threats.title: Lateral movement within the cloud network
threats.description: After the first foothold the attacker moves laterally to reach the DB.
threats.mitigation: Micro-segmentation, security groups per tier, IAM role separation, GuardDuty/EDR, network detection.

threats.title: Admin account compromise via weak MFA implementation
threats.description: Phishing plus weak MFA (e.g. SMS, no number matching) lets the attacker take over any of 16 admin accounts (AND-node on whiteboard).
threats.mitigation: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) for all admins, reduce the number of admin accounts, conditional access, PAM with JIT elevation.

threats.title: Privilege escalation to DB access
threats.description: Admin or Jenkins-level foothold is escalated to DB-level access.
threats.mitigation: Least privilege, separation of duties, privileged session recording, regular access reviews.

threats.title: MITM / token theft on Microsoft services
threats.description: AiTM phishing or MITM captures session tokens and bypasses MFA.
threats.mitigation: Conditional access, token protection, compliant-device requirement, continuous access evaluation.

threats.title: Lateral movement from corporate to cloud
threats.description: Compromised corporate identity pivots to AWS or the DB.
threats.mitigation: Separate identities for admin and cloud access, no standing privileges, federation controls.

threats.title: Compromised Jenkins leads to privilege escalation
threats.description: Vulnerable plugins or exposed Jenkins give code execution and access to deployment credentials.
threats.mitigation: Patch and harden Jenkins, SSO and RBAC, secrets in a vault, ephemeral build agents, no public exposure.

threats.title: Malicious or tampered build artifacts
threats.description: Attacker modifies pipeline or artifacts deployed to the Payment Server.
threats.mitigation: Signed artifacts, protected branches, pipeline-as-code review, SLSA provenance.

threats.title: Interception of customer traffic
threats.description: Network attacker (MITM) reads or alters data in transit.
threats.mitigation: TLS 1.2+, HSTS, certificate pinning.

threats.title: Request tampering / replay
threats.description: Attacker modifies or replays API requests.
threats.mitigation: Signed requests, nonces/timestamps, server-side validation.

threats.title: Unauthenticated internal calls
threats.description: Internal service calls accepted without authentication.
threats.mitigation: mTLS or signed service tokens between tiers.

threats.title: SQL injection via payment server
threats.description: Injected SQL reads or alters payment data.
threats.mitigation: Parameterised queries, ORM, least-privilege DB user, WAF.

threats.title: MFA bypass or fatigue attack
threats.description: Push bombing or AiTM defeats weak MFA.
threats.mitigation: Number matching, FIDO2, alerting on unusual MFA prompts.

threats.title: Stolen deploy credentials
threats.description: Credentials stored in Jenkins are used to push malicious code or reach servers.
threats.mitigation: Vault-based short-lived credentials, restricted deploy roles.

threats.title: Staging used as a bridge to the production DB
threats.description: Staging has network or credential access to the production DB.
threats.mitigation: Block staging-to-prod routes, separate credentials and accounts.

threats.title: Direct privileged DB access abused
threats.description: A compromised admin account reads the database directly.
threats.mitigation: Bastion/PAM, JIT access, session recording, MFA on DB access.

threats.title: Publicly exposed AWS resources reach the DB
threats.description: Exposed snapshots, buckets or endpoints bypass app controls.
threats.mitigation: Private networking, CSPM, snapshot sharing blocks.
